content.summary: Azure Functions (Python) API that manages content sections, such as markdown blog posts, stored as files in a GitHub repository. Authentication is handled via Google ID tokens; content ownership is enforced per-creator, with an allowlist controlling who can write.
content.description: A serverless write API for quixotry.me's content sections. Items are stored as files with YAML frontmatter committed directly to GitHub; the API provides a unified interface for managing these sections.
features: Create, read, update, and delete content items in named sections via REST endpoints
Support for multiple content sections, each with its own schema, visibility rules, and storage backend
Google ID token authentication (Authorization: Bearer header) — unified path for both web app and CLI clients
Support for multiple Google client IDs via comma-separated GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID env var
Per-item ownership: author_email stored in frontmatter; only the creator can edit or delete their items
Allowlist-gated writes via ALLOWED_WRITERS environment variable
Legacy item support: items without author_email can be edited by any allowlisted writer; first editor's email is stamped as author
Slug auto-generation from item title using storage backend-specific logic
Published/draft state toggled via frontmatter field for public sections
Optional description field for drafts; items can be saved without a description
CLI authentication via Google OAuth InstalledAppFlow with cached ID tokens and updated scope

architecture.overview: Azure Functions v2 app (Python) deployed to a Consumption plan. Each HTTP trigger handles one REST operation. Content is organized into named sections, each with its own schema, visibility rules, and storage backend. The default storage backend is GitHub, where items are stored as files. Auth uses google-auth to validate Google ID tokens server-side; no session state is maintained.
keyPoints: Content is organized into sections (e.g., 'writing'), each with its own schema and storage backend
Storage is GitHub by default — each item is a .md file with YAML frontmatter in skarumbu/quixotry repo
Google ID token validation via google.oauth2.id_token.verify_oauth2_token against multiple client IDs in GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID env var
ALLOWED_WRITERS env var (comma-separated emails) gates POST; PUT/DELETE further enforce per-item ownership via author_email frontmatter field
No Azure Easy Auth — all auth is application-level; Microsoft identity provider is disabled on the Function App
python-frontmatter used to parse and serialize YAML + markdown body; storage backends handle slug generation and versioning
Description field is optional for drafts, allowing items to be saved without it
CLI uses Google OAuth InstalledAppFlow for authentication, caching ID tokens locally for reuse, with updated scope to https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email

dataFlow.label: Web app / CLI sends request
sublines: Section and item identifiers in URL path

dataFlow.label: Azure Function validates Google ID token
sublines: google-auth verifies token signature and audience

dataFlow.label: Section resolution and validation
sublines: Resolves section-specific schema, storage backend, and visibility rules

dataFlow.label: Ownership / allowlist check
sublines: POST: email must be in ALLOWED_WRITERS
PUT/DELETE: requester must match author_email (or be in allowlist for legacy items)
Private sections require allowlist membership for all operations, including reads

dataFlow.label: Storage backend read/write
sublines: Storage backend (e.g., GitHub) reads or commits files
File content is YAML frontmatter + markdown body

dataFlow.label: Response returned to client
sublines: JSON with item data on reads
